claim.quote: Evidence for High-Energy Extraterrestrial Neutrinos at the IceCube Detector

date.note: arXiv v1 submission date. Published as Science 342, 1242856 (2013); the journal issue date was not read from a fetched source, so the verifiable preprint date is recorded.
date.quote: [Submitted on 20 Nov 2013 ( v1 ), last revised 16 Dec 2013 (this version, v2)]

key_value_text: 28 events, purely atmospheric origin rejected at 4σ
name: Evidence for high-energy extraterrestrial neutrinos

significance.quote: Combined, both searches reject a purely atmospheric origin for the twenty-eight events at the $4\sigma$ level.

summary.plain: IceCube found 28 neutrinos far too energetic to have been made in Earth's atmosphere, the first solid sign that neutrinos reach us from far outside our solar system.
summary.technical: All-sky search for high-energy neutrino interactions starting inside the detector, May 2010 – May 2012. Twenty-eight events between ~30 TeV and 1.2 PeV reject a purely atmospheric origin at 4σ, with flavours, directions and energies consistent with an extraterrestrial component.

title: Evidence for High-Energy Extraterrestrial Neutrinos at the IceCube Detector
why_it_matters: Opened high-energy neutrino astronomy: the first evidence for a diffuse flux of neutrinos of astrophysical origin.
